 Judgment

Wife and son of Mahadevappa S/o Pappanna filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of Tipper Lorry No.KA-09-D-3027, alleging that on 17.10.2023 at about 8.40 a.m., when riding bike No.KA-45-R-1173 on Ring road, Royal Inn Signal junction/KRS Ring Road junction, Mysore city turning towards right by furnishing indicator, driver of a Tipper Lorry No.KA-09-D-3027 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to Scooter, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Mahadevappa, who succumbed to the injuries on the way to Hospital.
SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 2.

As on the date of the accident Mahadevappa being aged about 58 years use to earn Rs.19,404/-
per month by working as Security Guard at Royal India Securitaus and use to contribute entire income to the family.

3. Regarding the accident V.V.Puram Traffic Police, Mysore registered a case in Crime No.227/2023 against driver of Tipper Lorry for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) IPC.
4.

In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through his Advocate filed written statement denying the allegations regarding the reason and mode of the accident, age, occupation and income of deceased.
5. Inspite of service of the notice, respondent No.1 owner of the Tipper Lorry remained absent.

6. On the basis of the pleadings, on 19.07.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 17.10.2023 at about 08.40 a.m., on ring road at KRS Road junction, Royal inn signal, Metagahalli area, Mysore city, in view of the negligent use of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-09-D-3027 accident taken place resulting in the death of Mahadevappa S/o Pappannaiah?
 SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 Manjula V vs M/S M M G Industries Pvt Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143557517/
2  2.

7. On 19.7.2024, 31.7.2024, 07.8.2024, petitioner No.1 Manjula deposed as PW1 and produced 14 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused entire records.

9. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under: -
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.12,73,036/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., as compensation, Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

In the evidence affidavit, PW1 Manjula W/o Mahadevappa stated that on 17.10.2023 at about 8.40 a.m., when Mahadevappa was riding a bike No. KA-45-R-1173 on ring road at Royal Inn signal junction/ SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 KRS road junction, Mysuru city turning towards right by furnishing indicator, driver of a Tipper Lorry No.KA-09-D- 3027 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to rear part of the bike thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Mahadevappa, who succumbed to the injuries on the way of Hospital.
11. In the written statement, respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding the reason and mode of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination, PW1 stated that she never witnessed the accident.

13. Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.227/2023 registered by V.V.Puram Traffic Police, Mysuru against driver of Tipper Lorry No.KA- 09-D-3027 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC., regarding the accident taken place on 17.10.2023 at 08.40 hours due to dashing of the Tipper Lorry No.KA--09-D-3027 to the bike No.KA- 45-R-1173 rode by Mahadevappa on the basis of the complaint presented by Smt.
Manjula W/o Mahadevappa SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 (PW.1)
. Ex .
P.2 is the copy of the PM Report.
Ex.P3 is the Inquest mahazar.
Ex.P4 is the copy of the spot mahazar.

Ex.P5 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident in which it is noted that on the junction of the four roads accident taken place at the western edge of the junction between motorcycle and the tipper lorry which are running in the same direction towards south.
Ex.P6 is the Motor Vehicle Accident Report.

Ex.P7 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by V.V.Puram Traffic police in Crime No.227/2023 against Ravi A.N. S/o Ningegowda, the driver of a Tipper Lorry No.KA-09-D-3027 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC.

Hence, I have concluded that on 17.10.2023 at 8.40 AM when Mahadevappa rode the bike No. KA-45-R- SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 1173 on ring road at Royal Inn signal junction/KRS road junction,
Mysuru city turning towards right by furnishing indicator, Ravi A.N. S/o Ningegowda negligently drove the Tipper Lorry No.KA-09-D-3027 dashed the same to the bike, thereby caused accident,
caused grievous injuries to the Mahadevappa, who succumbed to the injuries on the way to Hospital.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

15. Issue No.2: In the lengthy arguments, learned advocate appearing for the petitioners by analyzing the evidence affidavit in the file requested to award compensation as claimed in the petition.
16.

In the lengthy arguments of learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 insurance company by analyzing the evidence available in the file submitted that petitioner No.2 major son of deceased Mahadevappa is not entitle to receive compensation under the head of dependency by relying on the following judgments: -
a) AIR 2007 SC 1474 - Smt. Manjuri Bera vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. DD 30.03.2007 SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 b) MFA 3661/2019 - Smt. Shakunthala and others vs. C. Nagesh and another DD 02.07.2021 c) MFA 6818/2019 - Smt. Puttamma and others vs. The MD, KSRTC DD 01.07.2021

sentences.text: In the light of the judgments cited above, with reference to the submission made on behalf of both the parties I have appreciated the material available on the file.

17. In the evidence PW.1 stated that as on the date of accident Mahadevappa being aged about 58 years use to earn Rs.19,404/- pm by working as Security Guard and use to contribute entire income to the family.
18. In the written statement, respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding the age, occupation and income of the deceased.

In the cross- examination PW.1 stated that as on the date of accident her husband use to work as Security Guard at BML Company and since last 10 years as on the date of accident her husband worked as security guard in the same company for monthly salary of Rs.17,000/- to Rs.19,000/-.

PW.1 admitted that as per Ex.P13 pay slip Rs.4,004/-
is the OT rate and in the pay slip nothing has been SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 mentioned about basic wages.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident her husband never earning Rs.19,404/- pm and she never spent Rs.1,00,000/- for funeral etc.

sentences.text: In the police records, age of the deceased is noted as 58 years as on the date of accident.

In the copy of the Transfer Certificate marked at Ex.P8, Driving Licence marked at Ex.P12 date of birth of Mahadevappa is noted as 10.06.1966.
20.

In Ex.P13 salary slip for the month of September 2023, basic salary and OT rate of Mahadevappa are mentioned as Rs.15,400/- and Rs.4,004/- respectively total salary is noted as Rs.19,404/-.
21.
In this case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by PW.1 regarding age, occupation and income of of the deceased.

Hence, I have calculated the compensation under the head of loss of dependency in the following terms: -
Sl. Particulars Amount in No. Rs.
1. Age of the deceased Mahadevappa as on the date of accident 57 years 4 months SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 2.

Income of the deceased as on the date of 16,000/-
accident 3. 1/3rd deduction towards personal 5,331/-
expenses 4. Balance 10,667/-
5. 10,667/- x 12 x 9 11,52,036/-

Hence, I award Rs.11,52,036/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.14,500/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.14,500/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.88,000/- (Rs.44,000/- x 2) towards loss of consortium.
Hence, I award Rs.12,73,036/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., to the petitioners as compensation.
21.

In the written statement, the respondent No.2 insurance company admitted subsistence of the policy marked with respect to Tipper Lorry No. KA-09-P-3027 as on the date of accident and sought permission to defend the case under Sec. 170 of IMV Act.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 owner of Tipper Lorry No. KA-13-P-1736 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that respondent No.1 and 2 owner of tipper SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 lorry liable are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

sentences.text: The respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally liable to pay Rs.12,73,036/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2 insurer of the Tipper Lorry No. KA-13-P-1736 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within three months from today.
Compensation and interest are distributed among the petitioners at the ratio of 90:10.

After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% of the compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of the petitioner No.1 V. Manjula and entire compensation SCCH-1 MVC No.7937/2023 amount to petitioner No.2 Lohith may be released by crediting the same to their bank account directly.
Surplus compensation and interest allotted in favour of V. Manjula W/o Mahadevappa shall be deposited in any bank in her name for a period of one year without permitting to create any encumbrance.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
